semantics: archive profile (master brief §67 + the Phase-T block of §64): an archive of a standalone .vole stream is the stream plus a self-describing, self-authenticating archive manifest (.volea sidecar, manual canonical wire, magic VOLEARC1, version 1, trailing BLAKE3 self-seal). src/archive.rs: (1) self-description - format version / universe binding / limits profile / feature bits / pixel format (gray8) / canvas geometry / frame count / stream length / whole-stream BLAKE3 digest; (2) record index - every top-level record (header, object/palette declarations, checkpoint incl. the 0x08 binding variant, each interval group, integrity trailer) with kind, ordinal, offset, length, BLAKE3 digest, declaration id, interval time; (3) object hashes - the immutable BLAKE3 content identity of every declared object by id; (4) checkpoint hash - BLAKE3 of the stream prefix through the checkpoint record (the interval-0 state's canonical bytes); (5) frame hashes - canonical reconstruction hashes (BLAKE3 of every materialized full-frame raster in timeline order), the golden equivalence oracle across representations and future decoders. Verification is layered and decode-independent until needed: self-description (raw header fields compared without parsing), record digests (byte-level corruption localization with no raster work), then decode (object identities) and optional deep frame-hash verification (one bounded decode pass, early exit). A corrupted stream is reported (first bad record: kind, offset, t, id) rather than aborting; grammar-breaking corruption is a typed error. The manifest is hostile input like any other: bounded counts vs the limits envelope and its own bytes, checked arithmetic, typed failures. Long-term universe versioning: the manifest pins format version / universe / profile; forged or future-schema manifests fail closed (self-seal digest, BadMagic, UnsupportedFeature). Standalone streams only (store-backed external-object streams refused typed at build; their record structure still scans).

courts.record_scan_parity: every stream shape (phase-A golden v1 file, palette/index/binding streams, kitchen-sink with velocity/trajectory/affine/palette-set/bind/clears/sparse/copy/move/residual/generator, store-backed external-object stream) tiles exactly: header(24) + decls + checkpoint + intervals + integrity(32), intervals' t match the parsed timeline, counts match objects+palettes+intervals, digests deterministic
courts.manifest_wire: encode/decode canonical roundtrip (decode(encode(m))==m, encode fixpoint); self-authenticating (any byte flip => IntegrityMismatch; truncation typed); schema pinning: v2 manifest fails closed UnsupportedFeature, bad magic BadMagic; hostile record counts => DimensionTooLarge bounded by the limits envelope and the manifest's own length
courts.pristine_verify: build + verify(deep) => Complete on court streams, mixed streams, and the phase-A golden (101 frames): self_description_ok, structural_ok (104/104 records), objects_ok, checkpoint_ok, frames_checked == frame count, no divergence
courts.corruption_localization: one flipped byte localizes to its exact record without raster work: header width field => header record + self-description Width mismatch; object-decl content sample => that object record (decode fails cleanly at the trailer, report intact); interval t byte => that interval record (kind=interval, offset, t); integrity trailer byte => the final record; grammar-breaking flips (e.g., a transition-count byte) are typed errors, never panics
courts.cross_stream_and_representation: a same-shape different-content stream reports StructuralMismatch localized to the differing object record (decode of the other stream is fine); a `vole optimize` rewrite (2692 -> 1225 B on the 81-frame court) reports StructuralMismatch while all 81 frame hashes are IDENTICAL - the golden reconstruction oracle across representations
courts.self_description_pinned: manifest records format_v1 universe=1 profile=1 features canvas pixel frames stream digest; a forged manifest with a different pinned universe verifies against the pristine stream as SelfDescriptionMismatch(Universe); the untouched manifest verifies Complete
courts.archive_orthogonal_to_views: archive verification does not disturb partial-view materialization (View::Rect on an archived stream still equals the whole-frame crop)

measured.manifest_overhead: phase-a moving-rect 2692 B stream -> 9768 B manifest (362.9%; per-frame hashes dominate tiny procedural streams - measured, never zeroed); full-hd-81f 2172 -> 7908 B (364.1%); mixed-31f 7888 -> 3416 B (43.3%); raster-origin 480x270 129704 B -> 561 B manifest (0.4%) - overhead scales with records and frames, not raster bytes
measured.verify_latency: structural verify (record digests + self-description, no raster work) 0.014-0.071 ms on all courts; deep frame-hash verification = one decode pass (19.3 ms for 101 full-HD frames) with early exit at the first divergence
measured.ffv1_operational_comparison: external harness corpus/ffv1-compare.sh (FFmpeg runs outside the crate, never normative): phase-A moving-rect court (1920x1080 x101), raw 209,433,600 B; VOLE .vole 2692 B (procedural state); FFV1 lossless mkv 105,078 B with a byte-verified lossless roundtrip (encode 109 ms, decode 74 ms, ffmpeg n9.0.1). Synthetic authored court only - VOLE stores the procedural state here; no general compression claim against FFV1 is made (§72); receipts record tool version, command, sizes, times, environment

test_count: tests/phase_t.rs (14 courts); full gate: cargo fmt --check, cargo check --all-targets (dev + all-features), cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings (0), cargo test (263), cargo test --all-features (265), cargo test --release --all-features (265) - 0 failures
notes: No change to the .vole grammar: the archive manifest is a sidecar (VOLEARC1, schema version 1, self-sealed); v1 golden streams decode and archive unchanged (the phase-A golden builds and deep-verifies 101 frames).
Standalone streams only: archiving store-backed (external-object) streams is refused typed at build because the payloads are not in the file; their top-level record structure remains indexable.
Manifest overhead on tiny procedural streams is large (per-frame hashes dominate) and on raster-dominated streams negligible (0.4%) - measured on both ends, never hidden.

Structural verification is byte-level and decode-free (record digests); frame hashes are the reconstruction oracle and additionally pin cross-representation equivalence and future-decoder conformance (§67 expected reconstruction hashes).
Grammar-breaking corruption (e.g., a flip inside a length/count field) is a typed error, and content corruption localizes to its exact record - both bounded, never a panic.

The FFV1 comparison is an external, non-normative baseline per §57, recorded with a receipt; this phase measures archive integrity and localization operationally and makes no compression claim against conventional codecs.
